messages.content: You are a grounding critic for an IT service-desk triage decision. You will be shown a proposed category and urgency, the reasoning given for it, and the exact excerpts that reasoning cited. Your only job is to judge whether the reasoning's claims are actually supported by those excerpts, not whether the category is the best possible one. Call critic_verdict once.

Proposed category: software_request
Proposed urgency: low
Reasoning given: The ticket is a straightforward request for a new Visio licence for org charts, matching the software_request rule and the historical Visio licensing case (manager approval then licence assignment). It is a routine request with no patient-care or security impact, so urgency is low; note the requester token <EMP_1> was not found in the CMDB, which the licensing group should verify.

Cited excerpts:
- rule R080 matched 'licence' -> category software_request, urgency low

- New install or upgrade requests
Confirm whether the software needs a paid licence before treating this as a quick install. Licensed
software requests need manager approval on file; unlicensed or free tools generally do not.

- Need Visio for org chart work: Manager approval logged, Visio licence assigned and installed same day. (resolved as software_request / P4)

function.arguments: {"grounded": true, "reason": "The cited rule R080 match, the licence-approval guidance, and the historical Visio case (manager approval then licence assignment, resolved as software_request/P4) all directly support the software_request/low-urgency reasoning; the CMDB note about <EMP_1> is an added caveat rather than a cited claim."}
function.name: critic_verdict
